title: Korean Railroad, Seoul, Korea (1 Nov 1945)
producer: Office of the Chief Signal Officer, U.S. Army
licence: Public domain: US federal government work: filmed by US military personnel as part of their official duties, so under 17 U.S.C. § 105 it is not protected by copyright in the US (public domain). In Korea it is also out of term: the Korean Copyright Act protects films for 70 years from publication, and this footage is from 1945.
licence_notes: NARA's catalog shows the generic 'Restricted - Possibly' copyright flag that it puts on most of this series. The reel is raw Army Signal Corps camera footage (the slates name Army cameramen and units), so it is a federal work. Low risk, but recorded here as-is.

contents: Seoul railway yard in the months after liberation. Crowds in hats and coats press around freight wagons, and families climb into packed carriages. Children look out of a train window, and steam locomotives build up steam and pull out. (Earlier in this reel, before the cut, there are distressing shots of destitute children lying in the station plaza; they were deliberately left out.) The archive.org item 'gov.archives.arc.19239' serves a file named 'arc.18132'; its content matches the 19239 catalog title. Silent.
